previous_description: An atomic policy evaluation unit consisting of a condition predicate and an enforcement effect (PERMIT or DENY), with optional obligation actions executed upon match. Multiple PolicyRules compose a SecurityPolicy evaluated in priority order.
definition: A single evaluation unit inside a security policy that pairs one condition predicate over the request context with a decision effect (permit or deny). It may also trigger obligation actions when the condition matches. It is the smallest construct that both tests a condition and yields an access decision.

distinguish_from.when: the element is the named, prioritized container with a target that groups and orders several rules, rather than one condition-plus-effect pair
the element is only a field/operator/value predicate that yields true or false and carries no permit/deny effect of its own
the element is the response executed after a rule matches (log, alert, redirect, rate-limit, mask), not the decision itself
the element is a static grant of an action on a resource assigned to a role, with no runtime condition evaluated to produce a decision

standard_reference: OASIS XACML 3.0 Rule element (Target/Condition/Effect/Obligations); NIST SP 800-53 AC-3 Access Enforcement
code_evidence: A statement in a policy language file with an explicit effect and condition, such as an AWS IAM Statement with "Effect": "Deny" and a Condition block, a Cedar `permit(...) when { ... };` clause, or an OPA Rego `deny[msg] { ... }` rule.

An entry in a rules array of a policy config or Casbin policy file whose fields include a match expression and an effect value (e.g. `p, alice, /reports, GET, allow`, or `{condition: ..., effect: 'deny'}`).
A branch in a policy-evaluator or authorization middleware that tests a predicate on user, resource or request attributes and returns an ALLOW or DENY decision, often with a denial reason string.

attribute_descriptions.name: condition
attribute_descriptions.description: The predicate expression that must evaluate true for the rule to fire, recorded verbatim in the source policy language or as a normalized boolean expression (e.g. "user.department == resource.owner && time < 18:00"). Always set it; when the rule is composed from AccessCondition nodes, summarize their conjunction here.

attribute_descriptions.name: message
attribute_descriptions.description: A human-readable explanation returned to the caller or written to logs when the rule fires, typically the denial reason (e.g. "Only owners may delete reports"). Set it when the code or policy emits a specific message for this rule.

notes: XACML Rule Effect allows only Permit or Deny. 'indeterminate' and 'not-applicable' are decision results, not rule effects, so the enum should drop them. No rule id or ordering attribute exists, although rules are said to be evaluated in order; priority sits only on SecurityPolicy. The 'mandates' and 'requires' relationships to Countermeasure appear redundant.
